body: Boeing and Airbus hold a combined backlog of 12,420 single-aisle jets yet to be delivered based on 2026 order numbers, representing more than a decade of production at current output rates, so an airline ordering a new A321neo or 737 MAX today would not receive it until the mid-2030s. Brazil's Embraer, by contrast, offers delivery of its E2 regional jets in an average of 13 to 15 months from order, because the E190-E2 and E195-E2 face a far less crowded order book. Yet most mainline airlines willingly endure the Boeing and Airbus queues rather than reinvest in the E2, because on heavily trafficked trunk routes a larger aircraft burns less fuel per seat and earns more revenue from constrained, expensive hub airport slots, and airlines that do move away from Boeing or the A320neo family heavily favor the Airbus A220 over the E2.

Waiting is also expensive: airlines financing dozens of mainline jets largely use pre-delivery payment loans, structured as interest-only bridges until delivery, so a 12-, 18- or 24-month delay forces the airline to keep paying interest on borrowed funding while no revenue-generating aircraft offsets the cost, with interest compounding at elevated market rates. A second fleet family adds costs in four places: pilot type training that cascades through promotion chains, mechanic training and tooling, spare parts and spare engines, and higher crew requirements for a small fleet, although an AirInsight study of the 100-to-149-seat segment put those commonality costs at about 1.5% to 2% of operating costs over an aircraft's life and found an efficient subfleet could pay back in about a year. Major E2 adopters so far include Porter Airlines, the world's largest E195-E2 customer with an order for 75 units, plus KLM Cityhopper, Azul, Binter Canarias and Helvetic Airways, while ANA Holdings has raised its firm E190-E2 commitments to 23, Japan Airlines' regional subsidiary ordered 16 with options on 10 more for first deliveries in 2029, and Avelo ordered 50 E195-E2 jets with rights for 50 more for first deliveries in early 2027. Build time, however, is not a delivery date: Embraer names component supply as its main obstacle, expects 80 to 85 commercial deliveries in 2026 and aims for 110 to 120 a year by the end of the decade, and the E2's Pratt and Whitney geared turbofans faced powder-metal quality problems that also hit the A220 and A320neo family, even as Embraer's grounded rate fell from a peak of 22% in March 2025 to about 1%.
en.summary: Airbus and Boeing hold a combined backlog of 12,420 single-aisle jets, pushing new A321neo or 737 MAX deliveries into the mid-2030s, while Embraer's E2 can be delivered in 13 to 15 months — yet most mainline carriers still choose the queue over a second fleet family.
en.title: 12,420 Airbus A320neo and Boeing 737 MAX jets are backlogged while Embraer's E2 takes 13-15 months to build

body: 根據2026年訂單數字，波音與空中巴士合計仍有12,420架單走道客機尚未交付，以目前產能計算相當於超過十年的產量，航空公司今天訂購一架A321neo或737MAX，要到2030年代中期才拿得到飛機。相形之下，巴西航空工業公司的E2區域客機從下訂到交機平均只要13至15個月，因為E190-E2與E195-E2的訂單簿遠沒有那麼擁擠。然而多數幹線航空公司仍寧願排隊等待波音與空中巴士，也不願為E2另起一個機隊，因為在客流量大的幹線航線上，較大的飛機每座燃油消耗較低，也能在昂貴且受限的樞紐機場時段中讓每班創造更多收入；而即使脫離波音或A320neo家族，航空公司也大多偏好空中巴士A220而非E2。

等待本身也要付出代價：航空公司訂購數十架幹線客機大多仰賴交機前付款融資，這類貸款在交機前屬於只付利息的過渡融資，因此交機延遲12、18或24個月，就意味著航空公司必須在沒有可創造收入的飛機可抵銷成本的情況下，繼續為借來的資金支付利息，且利息會以較高的市場利率複利累積。另起一個機隊家族的成本出現在四個地方：飛行員機型訓練會隨著內部升遷連鎖擴大、維修人員訓練與工具、備用零件與備用發動機，以及小型機隊需要配置更多組員；不過一份針對100至149座級市場的研究指出，這類共通性成本約占飛機全壽命營運成本的1.5%至2%，而效率較佳的子機隊約一年即可回本。目前主要的E2採用者包括訂購75架、成為全球最大E195-E2客戶的波特航空，以及荷蘭城市快運、蔚藍巴西航空、賓特加那利航空與赫爾維蒂航空；全日空集團已將E190-E2確定訂單提高至23架，日本航空區域子公司訂購16架並保留10架選擇權、預計2029年首度交機，阿維洛航空則訂購50架E195-E2並保留50架增購權、預計2027年初首度交機。但建造時間不等於交機日期：巴西航空工業公司表示零組件供應是主要障礙，預計2026年交付80至85架商用飛機、目標在本十年底前達到每年110至120架；E2使用的普惠齒輪渦扇發動機曾因粉末冶金品質問題受到影響，同類問題也波及A220與A320neo家族，但該公司因發動機原因停飛的比率已從2025年3月高峰的22%降至約1%。
zh.summary: 波音與空中巴士合計積壓12,420架單走道客機，新訂的A321neo或737MAX要到2030年代中期才交機，而巴西航空工業公司E2平均13至15個月即可交機，但多數幹線航空公司仍選擇排隊，而非另起一個機隊家族。
zh.title: 空中巴士與波音積壓12,420架單走道客機，巴西航空工業公司E2卻只要13至15個月即可交機
